323488.title: Felsner–Krawczyk–Micek conjecture for poset antichains
323488.historical_check: no prior mention of this ID in campaign results/ledger files (grep of results.json, SUMMARY.md, ledger.json, status.json under frontier/campaigns, 2026-11-04)
323488.review_depth: primary body read (arXiv:1205.1824v3: Conjectures 1 and 5, Proposition 4, Claim 6, Theorems 2-3, Propositions 16-17); exhaustive computation
323488.summary: MathDB states Conjecture 5 (poset form). Source proves w<=3. Computed f(2,4)=8 exactly: no 9-element 2-crossing-free antichain exists in Z^4. Reduction: gap-closing in a coordinate keeps the antichain and non-crossing properties, and Proposition 17 caps each coordinate at k^(w-1)=8 distinct values, so WLOG every coordinate lies in [0,q_i-1] with max q_i=R+1<=8 attained on coordinate 1. Coverage: exhaustive max-clique over {0..4}^4 (no forcing), plus layered transversal search for R=1..7 (coordinate 1 takes all values 0..R). Via the source's Proposition 4 this confirms the upper bound of Conjecture 5 at k=3, w=4 (matching the source lower-bound construction). No counterexample; a parameter-instance verification only (zero credit).
323488.mechanism_next: f(3,4)>=28 or f(2,5)>=17 heuristic search; exhaustive search infeasible in pure Python (box 27^4 / 16^5).
323488.prior_art: web search 2026-11-04: no resolution found; source 2014 JCTA version states open for w>=4. Bounded search only.

352002.title: Affine fully commutative element enumeration conjecture for $G(m,m,n)$
352002.historical_check: no prior mention of this ID in campaign results/ledger files (grep of results.json, SUMMARY.md, ledger.json, status.json under frontier/campaigns, 2026-11-04)
352002.review_depth: primary body read (arXiv:2109.09773v3 Section 4.1.3, Tables 4-5, Conjecture 4.5); computation; published version (Discrete Math. 346(12), 2023) not read (ScienceDirect 403 policy)
352002.summary: Reproduced Tables 4-5 exactly and extended: a_m is linear in m for n=3 (m<=7), n=4 (m<=6), n=5 (m<=6), n=6 (m<=4), with increments k = 12, 60, 280, 1260 = n(n-1)Cat(n-1) = (n-1)binom(2n-2,n-1). Mechanism validated computationally: G(m,m,n) = affine S_n modulo m times the sum-zero translation lattice (affine generators project to s_1..s_{n-1}, s~_n), so g is FC iff it has a unique minimal-length lift and that lift is FC (321-avoiding); counting these reproduces a_m and its length profile exactly for n=3,4,5, m=2,3. Full proof would need the heap/abacus classification of long FC affine permutations (Hanusa-Jones; Biagioli-Jouhet-Nadeau) plus an exact boundary count; research-scale with very high Lean cost. Conjecture appears TRUE; no counterexample.
352002.prior_art: web search 2026-11-04: no proof found; author homepage lists the Discrete Math. publication without a resolution; GWU thesis record 403 (not retried).
352002.mechanism_next: Prove: for FC affine w, unique-minimality in w*t_{mZ^n_0} fails exactly on families whose heaps are periodic; count per period gives n(n-1)Cat(n-1).
